channel.title: The Chronicle of Philanthropy - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Chronicle of Philanthropy (philanthropy.com)

item.title: Meet the Man Who Revitalized the Louvre’s U.S. Donors
item.description: Thomas Moore says curiosity, in‑person meetings, and strong boundaries matter more than polished pitches. His advice: lead with sincerity, protect your team, and make every donor touchpoint worth someone’s time.

item.title: How St. Jude Raised $4.5 Billion in Bequests in a Decade
item.description: Leaders say trust, technology, and high-touch relationships are the keys to building a planned-giving powerhouse.

item.title: Monthly Cash Payments Could Boost Disaster Survivors. A Maui Nonprofit Tries It Out
item.description: Proponents of cash assistance for disasters say it gives people agency over their recovery and flexibility to meet their specific needs.

item.title: Smart New Ways to Win Gifts From DAF Donors
item.description: Our best guidance on how to connect with donors and unlock giving from donor-advised funds.

item.title: Is Your Team Afraid of AI? Here’s the Fix
item.description: Leaders can create parameters for use, facilitate an open environment where people can try things out, and make learning easy.

item.title: How This Community Foundation Created a New Model for Disaster Relief
item.description: After Nebraska’s 2024 tornadoes, the Omaha Community Foundation brought donors, case managers, and partners together to speed recovery, fill gaps in federal aid, and build a durable model for long‑term disaster philanthropy.

item.title: 5 Ways to Build Corporate Partnerships That Outlast Budget Cuts
item.description: Corporate giving is shrinking, but employee-engagement programs can help nonprofits build relationships that stick.

item.title: 'Abolish Ice' or 'Lock 'em Up?' A Nonprofit’s Middle Ground Approach to Justice
item.description: With federal funding cuts and crime declining, the Vera Institute’s new president argues philanthropy has a rare opening to advance criminal justice reform across ideological lines.

item.title: Can't Afford an Executive? Hire One Part Time.
item.description: Fractional executives let small and midsize nonprofits punch above their weight by bringing senior talent at a deep discount. Early adopters share how it works.

item.title: Trust-Based Philanthropy Is Not on Trial
item.description: A single lawsuit shouldn’t be misread as a referendum on a philanthropic practice that's legal, effective, and widely used.

item.title: Shattered Trust: $21 Million DAF Lawsuit Threatens Donor Confidence
item.description: In a legal battle, a DAF sponsor is accused of cutting off access to an account and refusing to make specific grants. Experts say the case is highly unusual but could impact donor trust and DAF regulations.

item.title: How One Family's Bipolar Disorder Experience Led to $1 Billion in Giving
item.description: Ted Stanley, whose son was diagnosed with bipolar disorder, wanted to give his fortune to one organization where researchers collaborate on their work rather than splitting it among institutions working separately on the same cause.

item.title: The Hidden Cost of AI Productivity at Nonprofits
item.description: Research shows AI tools can lead to longer hours and cognitive fatigue. Learn how to set boundaries that stop the always-on churn and prioritize quality.

item.title: How Small Grants Can Bridge a Gap — and Lead to Big Changes
item.description: Cures Within Reach has spent two decades supporting efforts that many philanthropists and institutions ignore. Its hard-won lessons extend well beyond medicine.

item.title: With Grants Hard to Come By, Philanthropy Infrastructure Groups Evolve
item.description: Once called philanthropy supporting organizations, infrastructure groups are positioning themselves to be leaders in the field.
